newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr subdued, mood bearish after retreat.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr subdued, mood bearish after retreat.

text.p: The Australian dollar remained subdued at the midsession after surrendering more than 1/2 cent of gains in one lapse late Friday to return to its old range.

Local activity was limited by a bank holiday in Sydney, but dealers suspected the pressure would resume offshore as more long positions were abandoned. The failure to push past 75 cents and the resulting retreat through US$0.7400/20 support had sounded a deathknell for rally hopes and analysts saw a risk its five month-old downtrend could extend further yet.
A weak set of ANZ job ads data this morning also reminded the market that yet another rate cut could not be ruled out.
By 12.15 (0215 GMT) the local currency had steadied at US$0.7380/85 after edging up from an early US$0.7365 low, but was well adrift of Friday's late US$0.7442/47.
Traders said scattered bids had been seen this morning and there was talk of a lot more lurking under US$0.7330 and down to the 18-month low of US$0.7310 hit a couple of weeks ago.

But chart watchers were not so sure it would hold this time, predicting a new bear phase to US$0.7250 at first followed by a grind to the 1885 low of US$0.7070. A near term recovery above US$0.7440 was needed to forestall the trend and US$0.7505 would have to be cleared to signal a reversal.
Such a recovery would be hampered by lingering concerns lsat week's official rate cut was not, after all, the end of the year-long easing cycle.
Most analysts thought there probably enough monetary stimulus in the pipeline -- 250 basis points off official rates and considerably more off mortgages -- to ensure a pickup in economic growth.

But they conceded that with underlying inlfation expected to remain below the Reserve Bank's 2-3 percent target into next year and plenty of spare capacity in the economy, there was room to ease further should upcoming data disappoint.
And recent data had underwhelmed, with retail sales and buidling approvals last week both softer than expected and the ANZ job advertisement measure today showing a sharp fall.

Job ads, usually regarded as a reliable leading indicator of employment growth, fell 2.9 percent in July after a downwardly revised 0.8 percent gain in June. Trend growth slowed to just 0.1 percent and analysts saw a risk the poor result boded ill for the official labour data due on Thursday.
Median forecasts are for a 25,000 gain in jobs but even that would be a modest result and any less would keep pressure on the RBA and market interest rates in the short term.
The local currency was mixed on the crosses, being up at five year highs on the broadly weaker mark at 1.3764/76 from 1.3682/94 late here Friday.
It lost a little ground on the yen to 87.51/61 from 88.52/62 and on the Kiwi at NZ$1.1479/99 from a strong NZ$1.1527/44 on Friday.
